deep.reconstruction:
Setting (my reading). This is a one-unknown least-squares problem in Gauss's bracket notation, here written with round brackets and a trailing 2: (aa,2) = Σ a_i^2 and (al,2) = Σ a_i l_i. The image reads (αα,2) and (αl,2); the machine transcription has (cl,2). The page shows how an existing least-squares estimate changes when one new direct observation of the unknown is added.

Step 1. The normal equation for z is (aa,2) z = (al,2). In the margin Gauss writes p next to it, defining the weight p = (aa,2) of the resulting estimate. C is the solution, so C = (al,2)/(aa,2) and (al,2) = (aa,2)·C. The symbol D is also introduced in the margin.

Step 2. Add a direct observation z = D with weight n. Its contribution to the normal equation is n·z on the left and n·D on the right, giving [(aa,2) + n] z = (al,2) + nD.

Step 3. Substitute (al,2) = (aa,2)·C (implicit step, supplied by me). Then z = [(aa,2)C + nD]/[(aa,2) + n]. With p = (aa,2) this is z = (pC + nD)/(p + n). Gauss writes p under (aa,2) in the denominator, so the result is the weighted mean of the old estimate (weight p) and the new observation (weight n).

Step 4. Put D = C + γ, where γ is the discrepancy of the new observation from the old estimate. Then z = [(aa,2)C + nC + nγ]/[(aa,2) + n] = (pC + nC + nγ)/(p + n).

Step 5. This simplifies to z = C + nγ/[(aa,2) + n] = C + nγ/(p + n). The correction to the old estimate is the discrepancy times n/(p + n). The weight of the new estimate is p + n (implicit).

Purpose: a recursive update of a least-squares result when a new observation of the unknown arrives. The combined estimate is the weight-proportional mean, written as old value plus a gain times the residual.

Context. The previous page (4r) is a combinatorial enumeration of permutations and partitions of abcd and has no direct connection to this page.
errors: In the denominator of the Step 4 expression Gauss first wrote a D (or C) after (aa,2) and then struck it out. The corrected expression is right.
No mathematical errors. The implicit identity (al,2) = (aa,2)·C, i.e. that C solves the normal equation, is needed to pass from Step 2 to Step 3 and is correct.

results.what: Combining a prior least-squares estimate C (weight p = [aa]) with a new direct observation D (weight n): z = (pC + nD)/(p + n) = C + n(D − C)/(p + n).
results.modern_name: Weighted mean / sequential (recursive) least-squares update for one parameter; scalar Kalman-type gain n/(p+n)
results.usually_credited_to: Weighted means: Gauss and Laplace era. Updating a least-squares solution with new observations: Gauss, Theoriae combinationis observationum, Supplementum (1826). Recursive form: Plackett (1950), Kalman (1960).

results.what: Weight of a single unknown determined by the normal equation [aa]z = [al] equals [aa].
results.modern_name: Precision of a least-squares estimate (inverse variance ∝ Σa_i^2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary one-unknown case of updating a least-squares estimate by a new weighted observation. Gauss treated adding observations explicitly in his 1826 Supplementum, and weighted means are standard in his work. It is routine scratch work, consistent with known Gauss material.

checkable.asserts: The augmented normal equation [(aa)+n] z = (aa)C + nD, with (al) = (aa)C, gives z = (pC+nD)/(p+n); the expression simplifies to 0.
With D = C+γ, (pC+nC+nγ)/(p+n) = C + nγ/(p+n); should be 0.
The update minimizes the combined weighted sum of squares p(z−C)^2 + n(z−D)^2; should be 0.

transcription_corrections: '(cl,2)' should be read as '(αl,2)' (or '(al,2)'), the bracket sum of a·l, matching '(αα,2)' / '(aa,2)'.
The 'p' to the left of the first line is a marginal definition p = (aa,2) (the weight), not a factor in the equation.
In line 4 the numerator begins 'pC + nD'. The small mark before C is a correction of '(aa,2)' to 'p'. The 'p' written under '(aa,2)' in the denominator indicates substitution of p for (aa,2).
In the denominator '(aa,2)[-D-]+n' the struck symbol could be D or C. It is cancelled either way.
